newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CRICKET-AUSTRALIA CRUSH NATAL BY EIGHT WICKETS.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-AUSTRALIA CRUSH NATAL BY EIGHT WICKETS.

text.p: Australia completed their preparations for next week's first test against South Africa in style with a crushing eight-wicket victory over Natal on the third day of their four-day match at Kingsmead on Saturday.
Left-arm wrist-spinner Michael Bevan took 4-35 as South Africa's leading province in the domestic competition were routed for a meagre 112 in their second innings in 52.2 overs.
Needing only 78 to win, Australia began shakily, losing captain Mark Taylor for one and Matthew Hayden for four.
But Ian Healy (41 not out) and Matthew Elliott (35 not out) combined in a 72-run stand to guide Australia to their fourth successive tour victory.
Although honours were evenly shared over the first two days, the Australians completely dominated on the third day with an impressive display in the field.

Natal missed the services of Jonty Rhodes -- who was unable to bat because of dehydration brought on by a stomach problem -- and collectively they disappointed with the bat as they lost 10 wickets on the third day for just 91 runs.

Only Natal rugby union centre Errol Stewart, with an unbeaten 49 in two-and-a-half hours, offered extended resistance as pace bowler Jason Gillespie, with 2-14, and leg-spinner Shane Warne, with 2-25, placed the home side under extreme pressure.
"The first two weeks on tour have gone really well although we had a bit of a wake-up call on the first day of this match," Taylor said.
"But we pushed up a few gears today and we were a very good outfit in the field, I thought. Warney seems to be back and everyone else bowled very well. Things are going very well at the moment."
Warne, bowling with greater purpose than in the first innings, made the initial inroads by removing both openers cheaply in harness with wicketkeeper Healy.
The 21-year-old Gillespie, consolidating his claims for a place in the Australian test side next week, generated pace and bounce to dismiss Derek Crookes, for five, and Neil Johnson, for no score.
New South Wales all-rounder Bevan, initially struggled with his length then mesmerised the lower order with a subtle mix of spin bowling.
